title: Live-output disconnects during high-throughput bursts — root cause and mitigation backlog
creator: Ava Kim
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 we observed a production incident where streaming responses were terminated mid-stream for a subset of requests during a sustained traffic burst. Symptoms included TCP socket disconnects, partial token batches delivered to clients, and a spike in reconnect attempts that amplified load on the serving pool. This ticket captures the root-cause analysis, short-term mitigations already applied, and prioritized action items for a durable fix.
impact_summary:
- Affected customers: ~6 enterprise customers using long-running chat sessions and streaming for partial response UX.
- Observed error rate: streaming disconnects increased from 0.04% baseline to 3.1% during the 09:30–10:45 UTC window.
- Business impact: degraded user experience (partial messages), several support escalations and two customers reported automated retries causing duplicate charges.
- Latency: average token latency increased by ~20% for affected requests due to retry churn.
timeline_summary:
2026-02-28 09:25 UTC — Traffic surge begins (batch job releases + customer traffic coincident).
2026-02-28 09:30 UTC — First spike of socket resets and partial-token reports.
2026-02-28 09:40 UTC — Autoscaler observed a scale-down race and triggered pod churn in one AZ.
2026-02-28 09:55 UTC — Ops applied short-term: disabled aggressive autoscaler policy + enabled increased socket keepalive.
2026-02-28 10:15 UTC — Error rate reduced but reconnects continued; engineering began postmortem investigation.
2026-03-01 — Initial RCA complete; mitigating PRs drafted.
2026-03-05 — Canary rollout of patch to handle partial-chunk idempotency and reconnect logic started.
action_items: A1: Implement idempotent chunk IDs and resume protocol so clients can re-request missing token ranges without duplication (owner: Diego Ramos, estimate: 5).

A2: Fix autoscaler race condition that caused pod termination under transient metrics spikes — root cause: incorrect cooldown window + misinterpreted CPU proxy metric (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 8).
A3: Harden serving runtime to detect partial-token emission and mark stream as 'incomplete' so clients know to retry with resume token (owner: Diego Ramos, estimate: 3).
A4: Add end-to-end integration test that simulates backpressure + reconnects across kernel restarts (owner: SRE team, estimate: 5).
A5: Improve observability: add a Grafana panel for "streaming-deliveries" with per-token ACK rates, and an alert when partial-token ratio > 0.5% (owner: Observability, estimate: 2).
A6: Update client SDKs to expose transparently the resume token API and to implement exponential backoff with jitter to avoid retry amplification (owner: SDK team, estimate: 3).
A7: Run a focused load test that reproduces the incident pattern and validate fixes end-to-end before full rollout (owner: QA, estimate: 4).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: No regression in non-streaming endpoints and streaming success rate >= 99.95% across a 24h stress window that mirrors the incident profile.
AC2: Resume protocol implemented and both server and SDKs pass the integration test that simulates chunk loss + reconnects.
AC3: Autoscaler cooldown fix deployed and validated in canary; no pod churn observed under the recreated load pattern.
AC4: Dashboards and alerts deployed; on-call runbook updated with clear triage steps for partial-token incidents.
AC5: Post-deploy monitoring window of 72 hours with validation report attached to this ticket.
follow_up_notes: Decision: We prioritize idempotent/resume behavior over a heavy-handed 'keep connections alive forever' approach because it reduces surface area for future regressions and keeps cost predictable.
Trade-off: Adding resume tokens increases per-request metadata and slightly more memory for tracking inflight sessions; acceptable given customer impact.
Review feedback: PM requests that SDK changes are backward compatible for at least one release cycle; design to include feature-flagging. (PM: Leah Ortiz)
Operations note: Increased keepalive helped short-term but does not prevent mid-stream kernel-level shutdowns caused by pod termination. Durable fix requires autoscaler change + resume protocol.
Security note: Resume tokens must be single-use ephemeral tokens scoped to the request; security reviewed conceptually with Security (owner: Marcus Li) — formal review not required for this change.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Kim: Initial RCA attached. Autoscaler signaled scale-down prematurely because the secondary metric source (proxy CPU) reported lower load for short intervals. Patch proposed in infra PR.
2026-03-02 - Diego Ramos: Drafted server-side resume-token prototype and unit tests. Observability hooks added to count partial-token deliveries. Planning to open runtime PR tomorrow.
2026-03-03 - Leah Ortiz (PM): Prioritize SDK compatibility and create a rollout plan with customers who filed tickets. Want to include a communication plan for affected customers.
2026-03-05 - Marcus Li (Security): Reviewed resume-token design. Recommended token expiry of 30s and HMAC to prevent token forging. No formal security board review required; will attach design note.
2026-03-06 - SRE on-call: Canary of autoscaler fix shows stable pod counts under recreated spike. Still observing occasional client-level reconnects due to client-side retry aggressiveness.
2026-03-07 - Diego: Merged runtime PR to canary; enabling broader canary after SDK patch lands. Remaining items tracked in action items list.
2026-03-08 - Ava: Updating ticket status and schedule for follow-up testing and rollout; assigning A1/A3 to Diego and A2 to Priya.
